codes.meaning: A mark for a correct method, awarded even when the working that follows contains a slip.
codes.source: CCEA Further Mathematics mark-scheme key ('M indicates marks for correct method'), Summer 2025 Unit 1 MS p.2; corpus scan 2026-09-05

codes.meaning: A mark for accurate working — a correct calculation, reading or answer. We treat it as dependent on the preceding method mark, as the Mathematics key states for A marks; the Further Mathematics key does not spell this out, so the dependency is our inference and is flagged as such.
codes.source: CCEA Further Mathematics mark-scheme key ('W indicates marks for accurate working'), Summer 2025 Unit 1 MS p.2; dependency by analogy with the Mathematics key (packs/maths/exam-true/mark-language.json); corpus scan 2026-09-05

codes.meaning: One mark covering both the method and the accurate result of a single step.
codes.source: CCEA Further Mathematics mark-scheme key ('MW indicates marks for combined method and accurate working'), Summer 2025 Unit 1 MS p.2; corpus scan 2026-09-05

rules.text: The scheme prints the most common route; other valid routes are credited mark for mark by the examiners even though they are not shown.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Instructions (Introduction), Summer 2025 Unit 1 MS

rules.text: A slip carried into later working is penalised once: the later working is marked on the candidate's own value, and correct method after the slip still earns its marks. Two or more slips are treated the same way.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Instructions (follow-through marking), Summer 2025 Unit 1 MS

rules.text: If an error makes the question trivial or changes what skill is being tested, normally no more than half the marks for that part are available, and sometimes none.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Instructions, Summer 2025 Unit 1 MS p.3

rules.text: Examiners credit relevant knowledge and skill: one wrong table entry that spoils several values is one error; readings from an inaccurate graph are marked against that graph.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Instructions (Positive marking), Summer 2025 Unit 1 MS p.3

rules.text: A misread that makes the question easier earns only a proportion of the marks, at the examiner's judgement.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Instructions, Summer 2025 Unit 1 MS p.3

rules.text: Further Mathematics schemes carry no numbered 'General Marking Advice' list; the answer-line, crossed-out-work and significant-figure conventions are inherited from GCSE Mathematics practice and are applied as in packs/maths/exam-true/mark-language.json.
rules.source: Heading scan of the 25 FM mark schemes (data/papers/mark-scheme-lexicon.json boilerplateHeadings: 'General Marking Instructions', 'Introduction', 'Positive marking' only)

rules.text: When rounding is needed, answers are given to 2 decimal places unless the question says otherwise; values read from log tables are given to 3 decimal places.
rules.source: Unit 1 paper front page instruction (docs/sources/papers/further-maths/2025-Summer/FM1-Paper-66635.txt); research 02 §8.1 general advice (3 d.p. for log tables)

rules.text: All working must be shown in the answer space; partially correct solutions can earn marks, but a bare answer produced on a calculator earns nothing if it is wrong — and for some question types nothing even if it is right.
rules.source: Unit 1 paper front page instruction; CCEA Teacher Guidance 2024 (simultaneous equations: 'Sole use of a calculator will not gain any marks'); CER Summer 2024 Q11(iv) and Summer 2025 Q12(iii)

rules.text: Bold words in a stem name the method that is required; ignoring them (e.g. 'use matrices') scores zero for that part even when the algebra is right.
Use brackets when substituting, simplify before substituting limits into a definite integral, and check that answers make sense in context.
Mechanics uses g = 10 m/s²; schemes and Teacher Guidance are written with this value.
rules.source: research 02 §4.2 (SAMs and 2025 scheme use g = 10 m/s²)

feedbackTemplates.M0: No method mark: {reason}. The working mark that follows is not available without it.
feedbackTemplates.W0: Method mark earned but the working mark is lost — {reason}.
feedbackTemplates.MW0: This is one combined method-and-working mark, and it is lost — {reason}.
feedbackTemplates.ft: Follow-through (FT) applied: your value {value} from part {part} is carried forward, so this part is marked on your own working.
feedbackTemplates.method-lock: The question said '{instruction}', which locks the method to {required}. Your route is mathematically valid but earns no marks here (CCEA examiners: {evidence}).
feedbackTemplates.trivialised: Your slip made the question easier than intended, so at most half the marks for this part are available.
feedbackTemplates.rounding: Answers are to 2 decimal places unless the question says otherwise; {given} loses the final working mark.
feedbackTemplates.calculator-only: The answer appears with no method. In Further Mathematics an unsupported calculator answer earns no marks — write the steps that produced it.
